**Step 1 — Scene:** Spaghetti with a tomato-and-minced-meat sauce, grated cheese in a separate small bowl, and water. There is also a sealed Magnum-branded packet; its contents are not visible, so I have not counted them.

**Step 2 — Vessels:** The main plate appears about **24 cm** across: area = 3.14 × 12² ≈ **452 cm²**. The cheese bowl appears about **9 cm** across: area ≈ **64 cm²**.

**Steps 3–7 — Items, coverage, volume, weight, and energy:** The pasta and sauce share the same pile; their allocated areas below avoid counting that pile twice.

| Item | Vessel coverage | Area × average height = gross volume | Density → weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| Cooked spaghetti | 55% of plate | 249 × 1.4 = 349 ml | 0.8 → **279 g** | 150 | 419 kcal |
| Tomato-and-meat sauce | 10% of plate | 45 × 1.2 = 54 ml | 1.0 → **54 g** | 150 | 81 kcal |
| Grated cheese | 40% of bowl | 26 × 0.8 = 21 ml | 0.9 → **19 g** | 400 | 76 kcal |

The main plate is approximately **65% covered**; the cheese covers approximately **40% of its bowl**. No separately measurable oil is visible; any cooking fat is included in the sauce’s energy estimate. Water contributes no energy and is excluded from food weight.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **352 g and 576 kcal** is plausible for this moderately heaped pasta portion and small quantity of cheese. Visual uncertainty is roughly ±20–25%.
